clue.text: Island goat without ears

indicators.note: without here means the second word is taken away from the first, leaving the front part

parts.note: Capricorn, the tenth sign of the zodiac, is pictured as a goat
ears are the grain heads of a cereal crop, so they stand for corn

explanation.surface: A goat on some island has been born with no ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes CORN (the ears) from the end of the zodiac goat, leaving the island off Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian holiday spot in the Bay of Naples is a well-known island.

clue.text: Reporter's paper?

parts.note: a gun's bang is its report, so a gun is a reporter; the case for its charge was once rolled from stiff paper, which still bears the name

explanation.surface: A journalist's newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The reporter is not a journalist but a gun, whose 'report' is its bang.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff drawing paper is named after the paper casings of gun charges.

clue.text: Experts support the introduction of practical rates

indicators.note: the introduction of takes only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: aces are experts at something

explanation.surface: Experts back bringing in practical rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' in a down clue places ACES beneath P.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeds or tempos, as in setting the pace.

clue.text: Motorway in the opposite direction permitted to include parking, that goes without saying

indicators.note: to include means the letters so far take the parking sign inside them
in the opposite direction means the motorway's letters are read backwards

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
licit means allowed by law, permitted
P is the usual sign for parking

explanation.surface: A road sign on the motorway the wrong way permits parking, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's M1 motorway is written MI; 'in the opposite direction' turns it round, and 'to include' tucks the parking sign into the run, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood without being stated outright, tacit.

clue.text: Holder of short suit

parts.note: short means brief
a suit at law is a case

explanation.surface: Someone has a short suit, as in a card hand holding few cards of one colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short suit' is bridge talk for few cards in a suit, but here suit is a lawsuit. The printed enumeration (5-4) splits the word the setter's way.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer's or businessman's flat bag is something that holds papers.

clue.text: Pulse, we hear, or other vegetable

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: A pulse, or some other vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a bean or lentil, hence 'other vegetable', but it is a throb.
explanation.definitionFit: A root crop such as the red beetroot or sugar root.

clue.text: Participating in contest, as it happened

explanation.surface: Taking part in a competition, as it turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally entered in a competition item; as an idiom, meaning as things turned out.

clue.text: Agent works without end

indicators.note: without end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: An agent operates endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a verb, but it is a noun for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts for another in business, such as a land steward.

clue.text: Second crop ruined at the farm

indicators.note: ruined suggests the words at the farm are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A second harvest has been spoilt at the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal sense, a second mowing in a season, gives the familiar meaning of consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the new growth of grass after the first mowing.

clue.text: Put up monarch above City square

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T

explanation.surface: The king is placed over a city square.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen's cipher; EC is the postal district for London's financial City.
explanation.definitionFit: To build or raise, as with a building.

clue.text: He gets single insertion in guide to cookery books

indicators.note: insertion in tells us the single letter is placed inside the cookery guide

parts.note: a recipe is a set of cooking directions
single means one, the Roman numeral I
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone receives a single extra page slipped into a set of cookbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He gets' is a whole definition: one who receives. 'insertion in' drops the single letter into the middle of the cookery guide, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who is given or receives something is its getter.

clue.text: Dish that is to follow a piece of the joint, perhaps

parts.words: a piece of the joint, perhaps
parts.note: a slice of roast meat is a cut, one example of a piece from the joint
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A serving dish that comes after the roast is carved, at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is slang for an attractive person, not a plate; 'to follow' puts the Latin abbreviation after the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a good-looking person, like a looker or a sweetie.

clue.text: Countryman's dog returns — it's back inside

indicators.note: inside places the second reversed piece within the first
returns tells us the word for the dog is read backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: back tells us the letters of it's are written in reverse order

parts.note: the letters of it's, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man from the country sees his dog come home, and it is back indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces turn round: 'returns' gives RUC and 'back' gives STI, and 'inside' sets the second within the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural person is a simple country dweller.

clue.text: US politician's noted comeback by default

parts.note: read as note D: D is one of the musical notes
read as come back: the word come written backwards
to rat is to fail to keep a promise or deal, to default on it

explanation.surface: An American politician is famous for a comeback after defaulting on a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'noted comeback' as a famous return; split it as 'note D' and 'come back' (COME written backwards, EMOC). The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of one of the two main parties in American politics, opposed to the Republicans.

clue.text: Fashion notes with smart varied collection

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape, so these letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's notes describe a smart, varied collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed range of different kinds, a medley.

clue.text: Girl's letter giving the brush off?

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, here with its possessive s
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A girl's letter rejects a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the girl's letter literally spells out the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving something away contemptuously is treating it with disdain.

clue.text: Subordinate position holding a command

indicators.note: holding means the position takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a site is a position
to tell is to command

explanation.surface: A junior's position includes giving an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subordinate' is a noun here, a dependent state; 'holding' places 'a command' just after the first letter of the position.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependent state or follower under another's power.

clue.text: Travelling entertainment for passenger, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a taxi driver's fare is the passenger being carried

explanation.surface: A travelling show offers something for a passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: A taxi's fare is its passenger; the travelling funfair sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair moves from town to town with rides and stalls, a touring amusement.

clue.text: Produce an image about here

parts.note: re means concerning, about
present means here

explanation.surface: An artist makes a picture of things nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or portray in art.

clue.text: Choice goody discovered without a recipe

indicators.note: discovered without means the goody word is found on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a goody-goody is pious, so goody here means pious
rec is a dictionary abbreviation for recipe

explanation.surface: A selected treat turns up without a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'goody' is the goody-goody sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Of great value, select, choice.

clue.text: Leaders of European agriculturalists to specify common foodstuffs

indicators.note: leaders of takes the front letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Europe's leading farmers set out what ordinary food should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' marks the answer as informal: it is a slangy word for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial word for food or grub, as in a plate of tasty grub.

clue.text: Local trading centre having cereal returned to give away

annotationWithheld.why: Local trading centre having cereal returned to give away (6,4): CORN and SHOP are clear, but no clue word supplies ER; 'returned' would have to be both the letters RE and their reversal
annotationWithheld.clue: Local trading centre having cereal returned to give away

clue.text: Dentists' routines?

parts.note: routines are exercises or practices, and dentists' working tools bore teeth

explanation.surface: What dentists do every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Military routines share a name with dental boring tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated exercises or routines; also the boring tools dentists use.

clue.text: Stand in gallery absorbing moving role

indicators.note: absorbing means the gallery takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: moving tells us the letters of role are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor stands in a gallery, taking in a moving role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the role to OLER; 'absorbing' puts that inside the famous London gallery, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to put up with or bear it.

clue.text: Replenish overturned cup in front of the bench

indicators.note: overturned means the word for the cup is read upside down

parts.note: a pot is a cup or trophy
to be up before the bench is to appear in court

explanation.surface: Someone fills a cup knocked over in front of a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' in a down clue turns POT upside down; 'up before the bench' is in court facing magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill something back up, as with a drink.

clue.text: Author has small cottage in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the cottage within the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE
a crib is an old word for a hovel or small cottage

explanation.surface: A writer owns a little cottage in the commuter belt round London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's south-east, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer, especially one who copied manuscripts by hand before printing.

clue.text: Train an engine driver keeps empty

indicators.note: keeps means the letters are held inside the words that come before

explanation.surface: Train an engine driver keeps empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless, vacuous, empty-headed.

clue.text: Discharged with little money to assist

parts.note: p is a penny, a small coin
to aid is to assist

explanation.surface: A debt is cleared with a small sum to help.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is settled has been discharged.

clue.text: Little lad without a bottle

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the lad's name goes around the other letter

parts.note: Phil is a short form of Philip, a boy's name cut down

explanation.surface: A small boy goes without a bottle of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means 'outside', so PHIL goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass vial for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: Possibly able to speak in detail

definitions.note: a describing phrase meaning detailed, matching the adjective

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of able might be arranged another way

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone may be able to talk at length about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the word able to ELAB; the speaking verb follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: An intricate plan is worked out with many careful particulars.

clue.text: Urge boss to obtain security device

parts.note: to urge is to press
a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield

explanation.surface: A worker urges the boss to buy a security system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like an employer, but it is a raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap fastener that keeps a garment securely closed.

clue.text: Exhausted writer found in street

indicators.note: found in puts the writing tool inside the street's letters

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A tired author is discovered lying in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up, worn out, with nothing left.
